document_purpose: Master, source-verified reference for all vehicle physical parameters and mesh sources used in Can It Ford. Every number below was pulled live from a primary source in this session (not from any NHTSA_vPIC_JSON file in the project, those contain zero physical data, confirmed by direct inspection). This supersedes vehicle_class_research_summary_2026-07-21.json.
important_note: This data previously existed only inside a Claude.ai chat conversation. It was not saved anywhere durable. This file fixes that.
canonical_status_note: CANONICAL vehicle-parameter reference as of the 2026-07-23 reconciliation. Two other files carried this same filename and are now superseded: (1) reference_data/vehicle_data_master_reference_2026-07-21.json.OLD-4906B and (2) vehicle_geometry_research/vehicle_data_master_reference_2026-07-21.json. Those two were byte-identical to each other (MD5 26796981b0a65c113095a291f2a267a8) and, despite the shared filename, did NOT contain the physical parameters in this file. They held the older vehicle-CLASS-COMPARISON summary (AR&R limiting depth / DV thresholds, moving-vehicle instability literature, the proposed 4th vehicle class). That class-comparison content is NOT duplicated here; it is preserved at archive/superseded_docs/vehicle_class_comparison_2026-07-21.SUPERSEDED.json (see ARCHIVE_INDEX.md for the original paths). If AR&R thresholds or the moving-vehicle citations are needed, read that archived file. This file is the single source for physical mesh/vehicle parameters only.

part_1_L1_AR&R_threshold_vehicles.source: SAE Technical Paper 1999-01-1336 (Heydinger et al. 1999), DOI 10.4271/1999-01-1336, public PDF at eng.auburn.edu/~dmbevly/mech4420/vehicle_params.pdf, fetched live this session
part_1_L1_AR&R_threshold_vehicles.note: Weight figures are actual VIMF-measured TEST weight, driver-only condition unless noted. Driver is already included, do not add driver mass on top.

dodge_neon_1998.VIN_in_printed_paper: not published, printed table has no VINs for any 1998 VIMF vehicle

honda_crv_1998.class: proposed 4th class, small footprint / high clearance, NOT yet confirmed added to project

part_1_L1_AR&R_threshold_vehicles.vin_availability: The paper's own text states VINs exist only in an internal electronic copy, obtainable by contacting Dr. W. Riley Garrott, NHTSA/VRTC, riley.garrott@nhtsa.dot.gov. The printed table has zero VINs for any 1998 vehicle. This applies equally to all four vehicles above, it is not a CR-V-specific or RAV4-specific gap.

part_2_L2_MPM_mesh_vehicles_NCAC_CCSA.source: Center for Collision Safety and Analysis, George Mason University, ccsa.gmu.edu/models/, fetched live this session. Reverse-engineered from real, physically torn-down vehicles under NHTSA/FHWA contract.
part_2_L2_MPM_mesh_vehicles_NCAC_CCSA.note: These are NOT the same specific vehicles as Part 1 (no current NCAC model exists for a 1998 Neon, Explorer, or C1500). Recommended as the mesh-plus-physics source for the actual L2 render, self-consistent trio, real VIN and tire data where available.

rho_reconciliation.status: Both mass options are recorded explicitly below (replaces the earlier single FLAG). This settles the reference file. It does NOT authorize pasting one rho into a script: the collider-volume basis is still open (see volume_basis_still_open).
rho_reconciliation.formula: rho = mass / collider_box_volume, units kg / m^3

mass_option_A_MASH_nominal_target.basis: MASH 1100C class NOMINAL target weight, not the weight this specific mesh was built to
mass_option_A_MASH_nominal_target.note: An earlier 2026-07-19 entry divided by enclosed volume 3.543 m^3 instead, giving 310.47. The 310.47-vs-310.50 gap is purely the 3.543-vs-3.5427 volume rounding, not a second number.

mass_option_B_NCAC_modeled_RECOMMENDED.basis: Actual modeled weight stated on the NCAC/CCSA page for THIS 2010 Yaris mesh (weight_kg_per_NCAC_page above). Matches the geometry the mesh was actually built to.
mass_option_B_NCAC_modeled_RECOMMENDED.note: RECOMMENDED mass pairing: use the mesh's own modeled weight (1078 kg), not the class nominal target (1100 kg).

rho_reconciliation.recommended_pairing: Option B: 1078 kg (NCAC-modeled) at collider box volume 3.5427 m^3 -> rho 304.28 kg/m^3. Chosen because 1078 kg is the weight this specific Yaris mesh was actually built to, whereas 1100 kg is only the MASH class nominal target.

volume_basis_still_open.note: The recommended rho assumes the collider BOX volume 3.5427 m^3. A separate 2026-07-20 entry computed rho from the RAW MESH volume 6.8185 m^3 instead, giving 1100/6.8185 = 161.33 or 1078/6.8185 = 158.10. Which volume the simulation should divide by (collider box vs raw enclosed mesh) is a still-open coupled question. Do NOT paste any single rho into a script until BOTH mass and volume are fixed against a live grep of the actual mesh. Cross-ref SESSION_STATE.md line 28.

rho_reconciliation.recommended_pairing_CORRECTED_2026_07_23: Option A: 1100 kg (deck header primary source) at collider box volume 3.5427 m^3, rho 310.4976 (stored 310.50). SUPERSEDES the recommended_pairing field above. Two independent live reads of yaris-coarse-v1l.key confirm 1100 kg is the ONLY mass value the deck itself states, neither 1078 nor MASH appears anywhere in the deck. Both are secondary NCAC-webpage annotations, not primary source content. vehicle_params.py and the L2 sim already use 1100.0/310.47 as of commit 6d14dcb. Old Option B field kept for history, not deleted.

suv_2020_nissan_rogue.only_one_version_listed_on_page: no separate coarse variant currently shown, may need manual decimation for MPM particle seeding

still_open_after_this_file: Rogue coarse/decimated mesh variant, only the large 3.24M-element version was found on the live page, worth a follow-up check for a lighter version
Rogue tire size, not published on this page, would need a separate manufacturer spec lookup

Silverado and Rogue mass/CG/inertia values above are curb-condition test weight from the vehicle description table, not broken into CG height or moments of inertia the way SAE 1999-01-1336 does, those may exist inside the linked NCAC validation PDFs (2012-W-003 etc.) but were not opened this session
Tire rubber composition and wet/submerged-pavement friction coefficient, genuinely not covered by NCAC pages, still needs a literature pull
Whether to keep Neon/Explorer/C1500 as the L1 AR&R classification vehicles while using Yaris/Silverado/Rogue as the separate L2 mesh trio, or unify to one set, is a decision, not yet made
